_readme: Three-check audit of content/guides/*.json, 5 a night.

changed: Magadha capital: Rajagriha first, later Pataliputra
Ashoka's reign 268 to 232 BCE: added 'scholars differ by a few years'
Ashoka's edicts: 'earliest securely dated, deciphered' records (body and FAQ)
Nalanda 'continued', Vikramashila 'flourished' under the Palas
Mesolithic table row: from about 12,000 years ago, later in some regions
Harappan: 'most extensive of the early Bronze Age urban civilisations' (was 'largest')
UPSC FAQ: Prelims history of India; Mains GS I culture from ancient to modern times (Mains has no ancient-history item)
unconfirmed_recheck: Megasthenes/Faxian/Xuanzang: verifier 2 tools blocked; verifier 3 found them standing

changed: Indus inscriptions: 'on average about five signs' (Mahadevan), was 'most have fewer than six'
Indus non-linguistic view: 'many specialists dispute', was 'most specialists reject'
Kharosthi in use until about the 4th or 5th century CE (body, table, FAQ; Britannica)
Gandharan birch-bark manuscripts dated about 1st century BCE to 2nd century CE (was 'around 1st century CE')
Grantha from about the 5th or 6th century CE (body, table)
Nagari table: from about the 7th or 8th century CE
'nearly every indigenous Indian script' descends from Brahmi (body, social caption)
unconfirmed_recheck: Siddham in East Asia: verifier 2 tools blocked; verifier 3 found them standing (Salomon 1998)

changed: Calcutta University anthropology department: 1921, was 1920 (caluniv.ac.in)
AnSI: set up 1945, HQ in Kolkata since 1948 (began in Varanasi)
South India row: 'Nilgiri and other southern hill communities' (Soliga and Chenchu are not Nilgiri)
'Gond Pandvani' changed to 'the Pandvani of Chhattisgarh'
Bhopal Tribal Museum: tribal artists made the displays (was 'helped design the galleries')
unconfirmed_recheck: university list: verifier 2 tools blocked; verifier 3 found them standing

changed: Paper II bullet: the syllabus does not name the Fifth/Sixth Schedules or PESA; now 'history of tribal policies and development programmes, constitutional safeguards, forest policy and welfare programmes'
FAQ GS overlap: 'related themes ... constitutional provisions' (GS syllabus does not name the Schedules or forest rights)
unconfirmed_recheck: 250 marks x 2, 3 hours, free choice of optional: upsc.gov.in blocked for verifier 2; verifier 3 confirmed from CSE rules; re-read the official notification

changed: Blue board: 'usually carry a board' (no source for 'blue' or 'every'; CAG found signage gaps), also social hook, caption, reel
Social hook 'older than most Indian railways' replaced with 'The ASI has been at work since 1861.'
Survey 'wound up in 1866', was 'suspended for a few years' (ASI history)
unconfirmed_recheck: Superintending Archaeologists head circles; Hampi is a mini circle

changed: Indian Institute of Heritage named as the deemed university formerly called the National Museum Institute (IIH notices; ThePrint 20 Apr 2026)
PG Diploma kept as one year: ThePrint 20 Apr 2026 reports it was cut from two years to one
'Some universities' replaces 'a few universities' in FAQ
held: 'Very few universities offer a BA in archaeology alone' removed: no source counts them
University of Delhi removed from list of archaeology departments: no archaeology department found

changed: 'Written records' now 'securely dated, readable written records' begin with Ashoka
Cunningham 'published' (not collected) the Harappa seal (ASR vol. 5, 1875)
Antiquities Act 1972: export barred except by the Central Government or an authorised agency (s.3), was 'without a licence'
Excavation 'needs official permission' (licence strictly for protected areas)
Social hook 'a thousand years of history' replaced with 'the inscriptions of early India'
held: 'Pushed back by some two thousand years' softened to 'many centuries': sources disagree on the figure
Sarnath dropped from Cunningham's identifications: ASI history names Sankisa, Sravasti, Kausambi
'through its Central Advisory Board of Archaeology' removed: not confirmed in the Rules
FAQ: William Jones as 'father of Indian archaeology' removed: no reputable source
FAQ: 'Hampi one of the largest historic city sites' removed: UNESCO gives area only

changed: Taxila: 'sent to Taxila' (Ashokavadana), not governor
Pillar edicts: six at most sites, all seven only at Delhi-Topra (Hultzsch CII 1)
Rest houses attributed to Pillar Edict 7, not Rock Edict 2
Prinsep sentence no longer says he used the edicts 'largely' (he used Sanchi donor inscriptions)
Delhi-Topra 'set up in his citadel' (was 'on top of his palace'); Delhi-Meerut 'on the Ridge in north Delhi' (Hindu Rao detail lightly sourced)
Reel line: 'over 2,200 years old' (was 2,250)
FAQ: National Museum has 'a major Harappan gallery' (was 'the largest in India', unsourced)
Name 'traditionally traced' to Buddhist and Jain script lists
'about forty basic signs' now 'a small set of basic signs' (count depends on method)
Devanagari FAQ: date 'end of first millennium CE' dropped
held: Kodumanal removed from pre-Ashokan potsherd sites: not confirmed by checker A

changed: Four-field model now 'associated with Franz Boas and American anthropology' (early 20th century dating dropped)
Karla chaitya dated 'around the turn of the Common Era' (Britannica late 1st c BCE vs Dehejia 1st c CE)
Ajanta later phase now 5th to 6th c CE, linked with the Vakatakas (UNESCO); 'horseshoe bend' wording replaced
Udayagiri (Vidisha) caves 'mostly Hindu'
FAQ: early caves 'around the 2nd and 1st centuries BCE'
held: 'Well over a thousand rock-cut caves in Maharashtra' removed: no acceptable source; now 'hundreds'

changed: Thanjavur vimana now 'about 60 metres' (UNESCO 59.82 m; 66 m unsupported)
Reigns softened: Vijayalaya to about 870, Parantaka I to the mid-950s, Rajaraja I/Rajendra I about 1014 (UNESCO 1012 vs Britannica 1014)
Gangaikonda Cholapuram capital 'in the 1020s'; Srivijaya raid 'known from his inscriptions'
Decline dated to the 13th century (Britannica: Hoysalas from 1216, Pandyas 1257)
Natya Shastra dated 'about the 2nd century BCE to the 3rd century CE' (Britannica range)
held: 'Ministry of Culture has listed Chhau' removed: no government source found; now 'some books also count Chhau'

changed: Pali and Prakrit 'like Sanskrit' not the main language of any state (Sanskrit was wrongly excluded)
Expert committee named: set up by Ministry of Culture under Sahitya Akademi (pmindia.gov.in)
Sanskrit tradition 'about three thousand years'
Sikandar Lodi 'made Agra his capital around 1504' (Agra predates him; was 'founded Agra')
Iltutmish 'issued' the silver tanka and copper jital (jitals were struck before him; was 'introduced')
Ajanta paintings 'the best known of them from the 5th century CE' (Ajanta also has 2nd-1st century BCE paintings)
Chhattisgarh: 'Gaur Maria' renamed to the Gaur (bison-horn) dance of the Maria of Bastar
Thang-Ta: 'performed as dance' softened to 'a martial art with dance-like display forms'
held: FAQ: 'the Ministry of Culture has at times included Chhau among classical forms' removed: no official page confirmed it

changed: Baul: UNESCO 2005 recognition was on Bangladesh's nomination, now stated
Burra katha: 'storyteller with a drum' softened (sources disagree whether the lead plays a tambura or drum)
Fort types: noted that lists and names differ between texts (Arthashastra gives four, other texts more)
Gagron: 'ringed by two rivers' corrected to water on three sides where two rivers meet
Amber: 'from the late 16th century' corrected to 'from the 16th century' (palace begun under Bharmal)
FAQ Kumbhalgarh: 'one of the longest continuous fort walls in the world' softened to 'very long perimeter wall'
'the first free-standing stone temples' corrected to 'some of the earliest surviving' (summary, FAQ, OG, reel)
Western Kshatrapa conquest dated 'around 400 CE' (estimates range c. 388 to 409)
'largest quantity of gold coins in early India' softened to 'in large numbers and many designs'
Chandragupta I coins: attribution softened to 'gold coins show the two together'
Reign table header: 'sources differ' added
Buddhist Krishna-Godavari region 'for many centuries' (was 'about a thousand years'); donors in 'many' inscriptions (was 'hundreds')

Amaravati sculpture: much stone burnt for lime in the 19th c.; largest groups in the site museum, Chennai and the British Museum, with smaller groups elsewhere (body, FAQ); only the plinth survives on site (ASI)
Thotlakonda group 'near the sea' (sea view sourced for Pavurallakonda only)
Undavalli 'often dated to about the 7th century' (was 5th to 7th)
Srisailam panels: Vijayanagara dating dropped (body, site note)
Lepakshi 'built mainly in the 16th century'; 'among the largest surviving murals' and 'unfinished' kalyana mandapa dropped (body, social caption)
Bhismaknagar: 'early second millennium' replaced by 'proposed dates vary widely' (body, FAQ)
Malinithan dated 'between about the 10th and 14th centuries' (sources range 10th to 14th; was 13th to 14th)
Ita Fort 'often dated to the 14th or 15th century though some place it later' (Incredible India notes a 1688 view) (body, site note, social)
Ahom rule ended with 'the Burmese invasions and the British takeover of the 1820s and 1830s' (was 'British annexation of 1826'; Britannica: British rule 1838)
Rang Ghar: 'oval' dropped (sources say oval or octagonal) (body, social)
Kareng Ghar naming: now 'royal palace at Garhgaon' (district site uses Kareng Ghar for Talatal Ghar's upper floors) (body, site list, FAQ)
Majuli 'the largest island in the Brahmaputra' (was 'one of the largest river islands in the world'); 'communities have had to move' (was 'satras')
Da Parbatia 'about the 6th century' per ASI (was 5th to 6th)
Ambari layers go back to the early centuries CE (was early medieval)
Khaspur: 'last Dimasa Kachari capital' (17th to 18th c. dating unsourced)
Nalanda active from about the 5th century until the 12th or 13th (ASI 12th, UNESCO 13th) (body, site note)
Sariputra stupa 'Site 3' (UNESCO dossier term)
Patna palisade 'often linked to' Megasthenes' wooden walls
Didarganj Yakshi: same Chunar stone, 'its date is debated' (no longer implied Mauryan)
Tala figure: 'identity is debated, though it is often called Rudra Shiva'
Qutb Minar begun 'around 1200' (sources give 1199 or 1202)
Red Fort dated 1639 to 1648
Qutb mosque begun 1191 to 1192; iron pillar 'first set up elsewhere'
Seven cities: 'one common list (lists vary)'
Khirki 'largely roofed'; Mehrauli 'one of the densest clusters'
held: Sultan Ghari 'the first Islamic tomb in India': superlative not supported by IGNCA or scholarship checked; now 'tomb Iltutmish built in 1231 for his eldest son'
Social caption 'first Sultanate mosque' softened to 'early Sultanate mosque' (unchecked superlative)

changed: Se Cathedral 'built over the late 16th and 17th centuries' (sources give 1619 or 1652)
Capital finally moved to Panaji in 1843
Arvalem caves 'around the 6th century, date debated'
Ponda temples 'largely rebuilt from the 18th century', deities moved in the 16th; deepastambha tied to Shantadurga
Fontainhas laid out in the late 18th century
Rulers after the Kadambas: 'changed hands several times' (Delhi Sultanate and Vijayanagara were omitted)
held: 'Silting' as a cause of Old Goa's decline: unsupported
'Marble and' jasper mausoleum: material disputed, now 'a mausoleum made in Florence'
Usgalimal details (Kushavati river, 100+ carvings, laterite, labyrinth, recorded in the 1990s): no acceptable source; reduced to prehistoric engravings in Sanguem taluka

changed: Somnath: consecrated 1951, dedicated to the nation 1995 (not 'completed 1951')
Girnar carries Ashoka's fourteen major rock edicts, not one
Dholavira 'among the largest' (UNESCO 6th, ASI top five)
Modhera: built under Bhima I, inscription dated 1026 to 1027
Gujarat Sultanate 'from the early 15th century' to 1572 to 1573
held: Vadnagar 'from about the 2nd century BCE': sources disagree (ASI 3rd to 2nd c. BCE, 2024 study c. 800 BCE); now 'occupied continuously for well over two thousand years'
Sidi Saiyyed Mosque year 1573: Britannica gives 1510 to 1515; year dropped
Khambhat link to Red Sea and Gulf: unsupported; 'ports such as Bharuch'
'Same families of stone carvers served both': unchecked, softened

changed: Agroha occupied from about the 4th c. BCE to the 14th c. CE
Chandigarh the shared capital of Haryana and Punjab
Rakhigarhi finds: drains, houses, crafts, cemetery
held: 'Rakhigarhi site museum': not open (under construction); removed from museums and FAQ
'Asigarh' fort name and 'rebuilt in many periods': no official source; now 'an old fort, much of which was demolished in 1857' (programme link text unchanged)
'Planned streets' at Rakhigarhi: not in sources checked
Sheikh Chilli 'Taj Mahal in miniature' comparison: unchecked, removed

changed: Tabo founded 996 under King Yeshe-ö; tradition credits Rinchen Zangpo
Hidimba temple '16th century' (1553 unsupported)
Shimla summer capital 'in the mid-1860s' (sources give 1864 or 1865)
Dharamshala seat of the government-in-exile; Tsuglagkhang in McLeodganj
Pahari painting: Basohli (now in Jammu), Guler, Kangra; late 17th to 19th c.
held: Tabo 'one of the oldest continuously working monasteries': no source; now 'in use for over a thousand years'
Masrur damage dated to the 1905 earthquake: year unsupported; 'earthquakes have damaged them'
Kuninda coin dates (2nd c. BCE to 3rd c. CE): only non-acceptable sources; now 'early historic period'
Kangra Fort 'one of the oldest forts in the Himalayan foothills': unchecked superlative removed
